# Expected outcome of every con-leche fixture under `lean-inductive-models`,
# run as the Lean Kernel Arena runs it (`--type-check-input --no-output`, all
# generation routes and checks on).  Read by test/scripts/check_fixture_verdicts.py.
#
# Line format:  <exit> <class> <con-leche exit> <path>  [# note]
#
# <exit> is this tool's exit code (0 accept, 1 reject, 2 decline, 3 error).
# <class> is the verdict of Lean's kernel on the stream as written, and what
# this tool must do with it; the runner enforces the pairing:
#
#   accept   Lean's kernel accepts it; so must we (exit 0).
#   reject   Lean's kernel rejects it; so must we (exit 1).  Never 0.
#   scope    Lean's kernel accepts it; we decline an owner our documented
#            scope excludes (exit 2).
#   defect   Lean's kernel accepts it and we do not: a known defect, found by
#            this port and out of the DAG-safety change that brought it in.
#            Exit 1 or 3, never 0.  Fixing one changes its exit and fails this
#            table until the row moves to `accept`.
#   foreign  Not a conforming lean4export 3.1.0 stream; we refuse to parse it
#            (exit 3).  Lean's kernel never sees it.
#
# <con-leche exit> is upstream's own expectation (upstream/e2e-expected.txt,
# upstream/annot-expected.txt), kept for provenance.  It differs from the kernel
# verdict wherever con-leche is not Lean's kernel: it brings its own prelude
# (the hand-written tower streams mention `Nat` and `Eq` without declaring
# them), declines what its set model cannot yet certify, and rejects a few
# streams the kernel accepts.  The kernel verdict here was taken with this
# tool's `--type-check-input` replay, which is Lean's kernel at the version
# `lean-toolchain` pins; a toolchain bump that moves a verdict moves its row.
#
# The tower streams upstream writes without a prelude are rejected here for
# exactly that; test/fixtures/dag-towers/ holds the same towers as complete
# kernel exports, which is where they gate the traversals.
